partners.diseaseBName: mitochondrial complex I deficiency, nuclear type 4
partners.mechanism_chain: ACAD9 (HGNC:18) —DISRUPTS→ Fatty acid beta-oxidation (GO:0006075); Fatty acid beta-oxidation (GO:0006075) —DECREASES→ Mitochondrial respiration (GO:0045333); NDUFV1 (HGNC:7740) —DISRUPTS→ Mitochondrial respiration (GO:0045333); Mitochondrial respiration (GO:0045333) —LEADS_TO→ Lactic acidosis (HP:0002146); Mitochondrial respiration (GO:0045333) —LEADS_TO→ Encephalopathy (HP:0001295); Mitochondrial respiration (GO:0045333) —LEADS_TO→ Hypotonia (HP:0001252). Loss-of-function mutations in ACAD9 disrupt fatty acid beta-oxidation, which provides substrates for mitochondrial respiration. Similarly, loss-of-function mutations in NDUFV1 directly impair complex I of the electron transport chain, a core component of mitochondrial respiration. Both disruptions converge on reduced mitochondrial respiration, leading to shared phenotypes such as lactic acidosis, encephalopathy, and hypotonia.

Loss-of-function mutations in ACAD9 disrupt fatty acid beta-oxidation, which provides substrates for mitochondrial respiration. Similarly, loss-of-function mutations in NDUFV1 directly impair complex I of the electron transport chain, a core component of mitochondrial respiration. Both disruptions converge on reduced mitochondrial respiration, leading to shared phenotypes such as lactic acidosis, encephalopathy, and hypotonia.

**How to falsify it:** If genetic studies reveal that MONDO:0012624 is caused by a gain-of-function mutation in ACAD9, or if mitochondrial complex I deficiency, nuclear type 4 (MONDO:0032609) is caused by a gain-of-function mutation in NDUFV1, this proposed loss-of-function overlap mechanism would be falsified. **How to falsify it:** Demonstration that mutations in HSPA9 do not impair mitochondrial protein import or that the observed phenotypes (anemia, congenital heart defects) arise through completely independent molecular pathways unrelated to mitochondrial function. _(variant: Presence of pathogenic loss-of-function variants in HSPA9 with a frequency > 0.01% in gnomAD.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of HSPA9 in mitochondrial protein import could lead to therapeutic strategies targeting mitochondrial function for both sideroblastic anemia and the other related congenital disorder.
